name: Linear
team_execution_depth: Built explicitly for engineering ICs and small-team scrum masters. Issues are first-class with status, priority, estimate, labels, cycle (sprint), and project assignment. Cycles are time-boxed sprints with automatic rollover of incomplete work — no manual sprint admin overhead. Triage inbox replaces backlog grooming for inbound work. Acceptance criteria are written as native sub-issues or task lists inside an issue rather than free-text body — task lists render as inline checkboxes that flip status independently. WIP limits exist on workflow states but are advisory rather than enforced (a frequent enterprise complaint). Definition of Done lives by convention; there is no first-class DoD object. Time tracking is delegated to integrations (Toggl, Tempo). The execution layer feels designed by people who use it daily — every interaction collapses 3–4 Jira clicks into 1–2 keystrokes.
keyboard_command_ux: Industry benchmark. Cmd+K opens the command palette; nearly every action — assign, change status, change priority, label, move to project, create sub-issue, copy issue ID — is single-keystroke discoverable from the palette. Status changes via single letters (e.g. 'Y' for In Progress, 'V' for Done) without modifiers. The full keyboard map is browsable in-app via '?'. Customer testimonials specifically cite 'the command palette and keyboard shortcuts make it way faster to move around and do things'. Linear's keyboard-first ethos is the explicit reference point competitors are now benchmarked against.
ui_responsiveness: Local-first sync engine is Linear's architectural signature — the client holds a local replica of workspace data and reconciles via background sync, so navigation, status changes, and filtering all render instantly. Sub-100ms is the marketed and observed UX bar for common actions (open card, change status, filter board) and is repeatedly cited in 2025–2026 comparison pieces as the latency benchmark that 'reframes all comparisons' against Jira's 2-second round-trip baseline. P50/P95 numbers are not publicly disclosed but the perceptual gap is the dominant adoption driver in HN/Reddit testimonials. [uncertain] precise P95 measurements not published
real_time_collaboration: Live presence indicators on issues; cursor-position awareness in shared documents/specs. Threaded comments with @mentions, emoji reactions, and rich-text editing. Activity feed on every issue captures status changes, assignments, and PR links automatically. Slack integration is bidirectional — comments thread back into Linear, and unfurled issue links show live status. Native Notification Inbox consolidates triage, mentions, and assigned-to-you items; many teams report this materially reduces Slack DM volume for coordination.
mobile_experience: Native iOS and Android apps (Linear Mobile, App Store ID 1645587184). Covers core daily-execution flows: viewing assigned issues, status changes, commenting, triaging the inbox, capturing new issues with voice/photo. Sprint board ('Cycle' view) is present on mobile but with reduced filtering. Feature parity gaps vs. desktop are explicit — complex operations like building automations, configuring custom fields, or editing roadmaps require the web app. Offline mode is limited; most features need an active connection and offline-made changes can produce sync conflicts. Adequate for daily standup and quick status hygiene; not a substitute for desktop for planning.
in_tool_documentation: Project Documents are native — markdown-rich docs live inside Projects alongside the issue list, intended for specs, PRDs, and status updates. Initiatives also have an attached document. This closes a meaningful portion of the 'open Jira + open Confluence' loop for engineering specs, though it is not a full wiki replacement (no nested doc trees, no fine-grained permissions per doc, limited templating). Adequate for one-spec-per-project use cases; teams with org-wide knowledge bases still pair Linear with Notion/Confluence.
developer_experience: Best-in-class for engineering ICs. CLI is community-maintained but actively used. VS Code extension surfaces assigned issues and lets you change status without leaving the editor. Branch names auto-generate from issue ID (e.g. ENG-1234-feature-name) via 'copy branch name' palette command. PRs and commits referencing the issue ID auto-link and drive workflow transitions. Deployment status surfaces on issues via Vercel/Netlify/CI integrations. The defining experience is that a developer never opens a browser tab to update Linear during a workday — the IDE plus the PR description does it.
vcs_integration_depth: Two-way sync with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket is mature and per-team configurable. Magic words ('Closes', 'Fixes', 'Resolves') plus issue ID in PR description, branch name, or commit message auto-link and drive workflow transitions. PR draft → issue moves to 'In Progress'; PR open → 'In Review'; PR merged → 'Done'. Per-team workflow automations let admins map specific GitHub states to specific Linear states. Personal git automations let individual developers customize their own automation. Branch name enforcement is supported by convention (the copy-branch-name action) rather than hard policy. Considered category-leading alongside Jira's GitHub app — the reference implementation for VCS↔planning sync.
ai_agentic_maturity: 2026 benchmark. MCP server at mcp.linear.app (OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) exposes 25 tools for find/create/update of issues, projects, comments, initiatives, project milestones, and updates. Native MCP support in Claude, Cursor, and any MCP-compatible client. As of April 2026 Linear Agent can itself connect outbound to other tools via MCP — agents inside Linear can pull from external systems. Admin controls include allowlists and workspace-level MCP permissions. Penetration data published by Linear: 75% of enterprise workspaces have at least one agent installed, agent work volume grew 5x in three months, and 25% of new issues are now agent-created. CEO Karri Saarinen declared 'issue tracking is dead' on March 24, 2026, repositioning the product as an Agent Management surface. OpenAI's Symphony agent platform is built on top of Linear, providing concrete enterprise validation.
time_to_value: First productive sprint typically within hours. No mandatory admin configuration: default workflow states, default cycle cadence, and default priority scale work out of the box. Templates exist for engineering, product, design, and QA teams. Self-serve onboarding — invite link, create team, start filing issues. The opinionated single workflow is the time-to-value engine: there is no choose-your-own-process configuration to complete before teams can ship. Customer reports of 'started using it in under a day' are routine.
migration_story: Jira → Linear is well-trodden. Native CSV importer plus a Jira-specific importer that maps issue types, statuses, assignees, comments, attachments, and links. Field mapping coverage is good for standard Jira fields; custom Jira fields require manual mapping or are imported as Linear labels/custom fields. Rollback safety: original Jira workspace remains untouched, so a parallel-run period is the standard pattern. Community case studies (e.g. Cotera moving from GitHub Issues at 500 tickets) are abundant. The opinionated model means teams cannot fully replicate complex Jira workflows — this is presented as a benefit, not a gap.
deprecation_transition_risk: Low-to-moderate at the platform level but high at the conceptual level. No layer is being sunset. However, the March 2026 'issue tracking is dead' pivot signals an aggressive product reframing toward agent orchestration; buyers committing to Linear today are buying into the bet that the next 18 months of product investment shifts further from human-IC ergonomics to agent context-feeding. Some long-time users on HN expressed unease that the human-first UX investment may slow.
safe_framework_alignment: Weak. Linear was deliberately built against SAFe — there is no first-class Capability, no Program Increment object, no ART concept, no PI Planning event, no WSJF prioritization field, no cross-ART dependency map. Initiatives → Projects → Issues → Sub-issues gives three useful hierarchy levels but not the seven SAFe levels (Strategic Theme → Portfolio Epic → Program Epic → Capability → Feature → Story → Task). Cycles are team-local; there is no native overlap of team cadences inside a single ART. Enterprises running SAFe typically pair Linear with Jira Align or accept that Linear is the team-execution layer only and portfolio planning happens elsewhere. [uncertain] some teams approximate PI Planning via long-duration projects + initiatives, but this is convention not framework support
reporting_metrics: Lightweight but well-designed. Native cycle burndown and progress charts, velocity per team, completion rate, and scope-change tracking. Insights dashboard offers cycle predictability and throughput. Triage queue size and aging are surfaced. Flow metrics (cycle time, lead time) are present for issues. OKR/initiative-level rollup via the Initiatives view. No CFD out of the box. Reporting is configurable but consciously bounded — Linear avoids the 'every metric Jira can compute' approach. Best-suited for engineering teams; less robust for program-level KPI reporting.
customer_signal_ingestion: Native Customer Requests feature lets support/CS tag inbound Intercom/Zendesk/Front messages to Linear issues, with request counts surfacing on issues to inform prioritization. Not as deep as Productboard but materially closes the support→roadmap loop without a separate tool.
integration_ecosystem: Strong on the integrations developers actually use: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Sentry, Vercel, Netlify, Zendesk, Intercom, Front, Loom, Cursor, Claude, Cycle. Not as broad as Jira's 5,000+ marketplace. Public API and webhooks are well-documented; many integrations are first-party. Marketplace is curated rather than open — fewer apps, higher average quality.
community_vitality: Strong developer-cultural reputation; active subreddit (r/linearapp), substantial HN presence (multiple front-page threads in 2024–2026), Discord community, and indie-hacker advocacy. Public roadmap and changelog are active and credible. Stack Overflow tag volume is small relative to Jira (reflecting Linear's lower configuration burden — fewer questions to ask). No comparable marketplace moat to Jira's 5,000+ apps. [uncertain] precise community metric counts
self_hosting_data_residency: SaaS-only. No on-premises or private-cloud deployment. Data residency: US-hosted; an EU data residency option exists for Enterprise customers. Not viable for buyers requiring true on-prem or government-cloud isolation. [uncertain] full list of available residency regions
customization: Deliberately limited compared to Jira. Custom fields (added in 2024) on Business and Enterprise tiers. Custom workflow states per team. Custom views and saved filters. No custom screen layouts, no scripted automations beyond simple per-team rules, no custom work item types beyond Issue/Sub-issue/Project/Initiative. This is presented as a design value, not a gap — admins cannot create a maintenance burden. Enterprises wanting deep configurability bounce off Linear; that is intentional.
pricing_commercial_model: Per-user, four tiers. Free: unlimited members, capped at 250 non-archived issues and 2 teams. Basic: $10/user/month billed annually. Business: $16/user/month (after aggressive cuts — was $50 in July 2025, $29 in January 2026, $16 in February 2026, a 68% reduction in seven months reflecting competitive pressure). Enterprise: custom pricing, estimated $250–$350/user/year at 100 seats, $230–$300 at 500+. Annual billing required for paid tiers (monthly available at higher rates). Pricing is straightforward — no per-portfolio or per-project add-ons.
total_cost_of_ownership: Materially lower than ServiceNow EAP or Jira Premium+Align for equivalent-size teams. Implementation typically self-serve — no required SI consulting. Admin overhead is minimal (under 0.1 FTE for most workspaces) because configuration depth is bounded. Training is essentially nil — onboarding videos plus the in-app help are sufficient for most ICs. Integration maintenance is light because the integrations Linear ships are first-party. 3-year TCO for a 200-seat team at Business: roughly $115K with no implementation cost. The trade-off is functional ceiling, not cost.
market_perception: Cult-status among startup and scaleup engineering teams. Gartner positions Linear as a Visionary in adjacent quadrants but it has historically been excluded from the Enterprise Agile Planning Tools Magic Quadrant on framework-support grounds. G2 reviews trend strongly positive, dominated by 'fast', 'beautiful', 'finally a PM tool engineers like'. HN/Reddit sentiment is overwhelmingly favorable among ICs and skeptical among traditional PMO buyers ('great until you need a Gantt chart for your CFO'). Fireship's 2025 'Why every startup is switching to Linear' video is a cultural marker. [uncertain] exact 2026 G2/Gartner Peer Insights review counts and aggregate scores
gaps_vs_market_leader: Vs. Jira: (1) No native Gantt/timeline at portfolio scale — Linear's Roadmaps view does not match Advanced Roadmaps' dependency mapping. (2) Workflow customization is intentionally bounded — enterprise PMOs that need bespoke per-project workflows hit a wall (showstopper for some). (3) No native SAFe artifacts — no PI, no ART, no Capability, no WSJF. (4) Marketplace is curated and small vs. Jira's 5,000+ apps. (5) No on-prem/government-cloud option (showstopper for regulated buyers). (6) Reporting depth is bounded — no CFD, lighter custom-report support. Vs. Linear's own benchmark: Linear is the leader, so the comparison reverses for everyone else. Severity ranking: SAFe absence (showstopper for SAFe enterprises), on-prem absence (showstopper for regulated), customization ceiling (friction for PMO-led orgs), Gantt depth (friction for executive reporting).
